environment: Great Barrier Reef monitoring shows encouraging coral cover in parts of the north as scientists keep a close watch this spring
Queensland's big battery and pumped hydro projects push forward as the state chases its renewable energy targets
science: University of Queensland researchers make headway on new coral resilience and marine health studies
sports: Grand Final fever builds across the footy codes as Queensland fans get set for a huge finals weekend
stories.overview: Spring sunshine, reef hope and finals fever - Queensland is buzzing with good vibes this weekend

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer, glad you could join us on this ripper of a Saturday. We've got a cracking show lined up, reef news, brainy science and a big weekend of footy to get through. And I'm Jamie, buzzing to be here with you all. Honestly Alex, spring has sprung and there is just so much good stuff happening across Queensland right now. Too right. Grab your coffee, settle in, because we're keeping it all sunny side up today, starting with some genuinely good environment news.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Let's kick off with the reef, because there is some cautiously good news out there. Long term monitoring teams have been tracking coral cover in the northern sections and things are looking more resilient than a lot of people feared a few years back. Yeah it's not all doom and gloom mate, which makes a nice change. Scientists reckon a run of milder summers combined with reef protection work has given the coral a bit of breathing room to bounce back in places. It's a timely reminder too, with Queensland pushing hard on big battery storage and pumped hydro projects to get more renewables onto the grid. Every bit of clean energy we add takes a bit of pressure off that reef down the track.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Righto, let's get a bit nerdy for a sec, in the best way possible. Researchers over at the University of Queensland have been deep in the lab looking at what makes some coral colonies tougher than others when the water heats up. I love this stuff, because it's not just theory, it actually feeds straight back into reef restoration work happening right now off our coast. They're basically trying to breed a bit of extra grit into the coral of the future. Fair dinkum clever stuff. It's the kind of quiet, patient science that doesn't always make the front page but ends up mattering more than half the headlines we see.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, thanks Jamie. Look, south east Queensland is doing exactly what spring is supposed to do this weekend, plenty of sunshine, light winds and temperatures sitting in that lovely mid to high twenties most afternoons. Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast are all set for clear skies today with just the odd fluffy cloud rolling through, perfect beach or backyard weather either way. We might see a stray afternoon shower pop up further inland as the land warms up, but for the coast it's staying dry and pleasant right through the weekend. Overnight it'll cool off nicely into the mid teens, so a great excuse to get outdoors and enjoy that spring air while it lasts. Back to you two.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Big one this segment, because finals fever is officially in the air across the footy codes. Whether you're an AFL diehard or bleeding maroon and blue for the NRL, this is the time of year Queenslanders live for. It really is, the whole state gets behind it doesn't it. Pubs are packed, backyards are full of jerseys, and everyone's got an opinion on who's peaking at the right time. That's the beauty of grand final season mate, it brings people together over a snag and a cold drink no matter who you're barracking for. We'll keep you posted as the big games roll on.
